subject.title: [Feature]: Support for sandbox Docker parameters (--gpus all, --ipc=host)

question: Should OpenClaw expose host IPC for Docker sandboxes, and if yes should it be a narrow explicit `sandbox.docker.ipc` break-glass field instead of raw Docker argument passthrough?
rationale: The remaining request changes sandbox namespace isolation and the public config contract; automation can identify the shape, but maintainers must decide the acceptable security tradeoff.

options.title: Add narrow host IPC field
options.body: Implement explicit opt-in IPC support with schema, docs, config hashing or recreate behavior, security-audit/dangerous-flag coverage, and Docker argv tests while keeping raw args unsupported.

options.title: Reject host IPC in core
options.body: Keep GPU passthrough as the supported high-power Docker path and document host IPC/raw args as unsupported because they weaken sandbox isolation.

options.title: Design broader namespace policy
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers define one policy for IPC, PID, network namespace joins, capabilities, and other dangerous Docker options.

recommendation.title: Add narrow host IPC field
recommendation.body: Implement explicit opt-in IPC support with schema, docs, config hashing or recreate behavior, security-audit/dangerous-flag coverage, and Docker argv tests while keeping raw args unsupported.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent sandbox namespace hardening history makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the security-boundary choice.
